question: Why do pigeons bob their heads?

frame0.description: Big pigeon mid-stride on a city sidewalk, camera tracking it; the premise reads as a thumbnail.

loop.last_line: which probably helps them spot movement.
loop.description: The pigeon snaps a falling crumb and walks on; the last frame matches frame 0

assets.description: Pigeon cut into head, neck and body for a walking rig; legs, eye and brow drawn in code
Big close-up of the pigeon's head; eye and brow drawn in code
Scientist with empty hands in the same pose as g_hold
Small treadmill with a green button; belt slats animated in code
City street backdrop for the multiplane camera

beats.line: A walking pigeon's head never actually moves backward.
beats.visual: Normal walk with the camera tracking the body, so the head seems to bob. The camera eases to a stop and the walk slows into slow motion; a red dashed guide line pops at the beak tip. A white arrow pointing back appears behind the head and a red X stamps over it.
beats.camera: Tracking, then eases to a stop
beats.gag: The red X stamps the wrong idea

beats.line: It freezes in place while the body moves forward, then darts ahead.
beats.visual: Dolly in (2.5D, buildings blur). A new hold starts: head parked on the line, red pause badge above it; the body glides forward under the still head; then the head thrusts forward with speed lines and a new line appears at the new spot.
beats.gag: The neck stretches back like taffy while the head stays put

beats.visual: Dolly out to reveal the scientist thinking; on "balance" he squash-swaps to a one-leg wobble with a sweat drop.

beats.line: But when scientists put pigeons on a treadmill, the bobbing stopped.
beats.visual: Cut to the lab: scientist holds the pigeon next to a small treadmill, bread poster on the wall. On "put" he swaps to empty hands and the rigged pigeon hops onto the belt; on "treadmill" the green button glows and the belt runs. The guide line at the beak shows the head never leaves it; he swaps to clipboard and surprise.
beats.gag: The pigeon steps onto the belt like it's late for work

beats.line: Their legs kept walking, but their view never changed.
beats.visual: Push in to the treadmill as the scientist scoots out of frame; close on the legs churning on the moving belt; a sight cone from the eye to the bread poster stays fixed.
beats.gag: Its eyes never leave the bread poster

beats.visual: Cut to a big close-up of the pigeon's head; on "vision" the eye pops, the brow lifts, sparkles.

beats.line: Each freeze gives a steady view,
beats.visual: Cut back to the street, pigeon walking; viewfinder brackets in front of the head stay still during holds and snap at each new freeze.
Cut to the scientist holding a camera: it trembles, then locks dead still; flash on "still".

beats.line: which probably helps them spot movement.
beats.visual: Cut to the street, same framing as frame 0. A crumb falls; the head is frozen and the eye pops on "spot"; on "movement" the pigeon snaps it out of the air and walks on (loop to frame 0).
